title: Closure under negation and identification
statement: Fix $k\in\mathbb N$. For all natural numbers $n,m$, if a $\{-1,1\}$-valued function on $\{0,1\}^n$ has a polynomial threshold representation of degree at most $k$, then for every $z\in\{0,1\}^n$ and every map $\pi:[n]\to[m]$, the function on $\{0,1\}^m$ given by $g(w)=f((z_i+w_{\pi(i)}\pmod 2)_{i=1}^n)$ is also $\{-1,1\}$-valued and has a polynomial threshold representation of degree at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: n and m are natural numbers
f has a polynomial threshold representation of degree at most k
π is a map from [n] to [m]
replaced:
For every $k,n,m\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\}$ of the form $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(p((-1)^{x_1},\ldots,(-1)^{x_n}))$ for a real multilinear polynomial $p$ of degree at most $k$, every $z\in\{0,1\}^{n}$ and every map $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$, the function $g(w)=f((z_i+w_{\pi(i)}\pmod2)_{i=1}^{n})$ is also $\{-1,1\}$-valued and has a representation $g(w)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(q((-1)^{w_1},\ldots,(-1)^{w_m}))$ with a real multilinear polynomial $q$ of degree at most $k$.
Here $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
